Transcript:
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
[2] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's blue eyes widen and she lets out a bright laugh, leaning over the counter. "A friend? Honestly, I've been calling you that in my head since you walked through the door with that map today. Consider it official." She sets down her serving tray with a clatter and beams at the group. "Friends get a discount on drinks. Well, friends get the same price as everyone else, but they don't have to wait as long for their order."
The Guildhall's usual midday bustle carries on around them — the clink of mugs, the low rumble of adventurers discussing quests, the scrape of chairs on wooden floors. Fiana's smile doesn't waver, though she glances toward the quest board where Vallie and Domas have just finished making their announcement.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
[4] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression shifts, her smile softening into something more thoughtful as she leans against the counter. "Jasira?" She runs a hand through her short red curls. "She's... complicated. We've known each other a few years, and she's definitely a friend, but she's not the easiest person to be friends with."
Fiana lowers her voice slightly, glancing toward the tavern's entrance as a group of rowdy adventurers pushes in. "She's got this wall up, especially around anyone who isn't an elf. It's like she's trying to protect something, or prove something to herself. But when it's just us, or with Ellie and Dalan, you see the real Jasira — someone who gives a damn and would probably fight a dragon for the people she cares about." She gives a small shrug. "Just don't ask her about her tribe too often. That's a topic that makes her go colder than a winter in the northern hills."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
[2] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's blue eyes widen and she lets out a bright laugh, leaning over the counter. "A friend? Honestly, I've been calling you that in my head since you walked through the door with that map today. Consider it official." She sets down her serving tray with a clatter and beams at the group. "Friends get a discount on drinks. Well, friends get the same price as everyone else, but they don't have to wait as long for their order."
The Guildhall's usual midday bustle carries on around them — the clink of mugs, the low rumble of adventurers discussing quests, the scrape of chairs on wooden floors. Fiana's smile doesn't waver, though she glances toward the quest board where Vallie and Domas have just finished making their announcement.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
[4] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression shifts, her smile softening into something more thoughtful as she leans against the counter. "Jasira?" She runs a hand through her short red curls. "She's... complicated. We've known each other a few years, and she's definitely a friend, but she's not the easiest person to be friends with."
Fiana lowers her voice slightly, glancing toward the tavern's entrance as a group of rowdy adventurers pushes in. "She's got this wall up, especially around anyone who isn't an elf. It's like she's trying to protect something, or prove something to herself. But when it's just us, or with Ellie and Dalan, you see the real Jasira — someone who gives a damn and would probably fight a dragon for the people she cares about." She gives a small shrug. "Just don't ask her about her tribe too often. That's a topic that makes her go colder than a winter in the northern hills."
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie lets out a short, sharp laugh and slaps a hand against the railing, the sound like a crack of thunder. "Trust?" Her one good eye narrows, not with suspicion but with something else — amusement, maybe. "Kid, I don't trust anyone who tells me they're trustworthy. Trust is earned with blood, sweat, and not pissing me off when I'm holding your coin."
*She leans forward, horns catching the lantern light.* "But you've shown more spine than most D-ranks. You took on a job you could've walked away from and didn't run when things got bloody. That counts for something." *A scarred hand comes down on the counter between the exam forms, fingers curled.* "I trust you'll sign those papers if you're got the stones for it. The rest? Well, that's what the exam is for."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
[2] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's blue eyes widen and she lets out a bright laugh, leaning over the counter. "A friend? Honestly, I've been calling you that in my head since you walked through the door with that map today. Consider it official." She sets down her serving tray with a clatter and beams at the group. "Friends get a discount on drinks. Well, friends get the same price as everyone else, but they don't have to wait as long for their order."
The Guildhall's usual midday bustle carries on around them — the clink of mugs, the low rumble of adventurers discussing quests, the scrape of chairs on wooden floors. Fiana's smile doesn't waver, though she glances toward the quest board where Vallie and Domas have just finished making their announcement.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
[4] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression shifts, her smile softening into something more thoughtful as she leans against the counter. "Jasira?" She runs a hand through her short red curls. "She's... complicated. We've known each other a few years, and she's definitely a friend, but she's not the easiest person to be friends with."
Fiana lowers her voice slightly, glancing toward the tavern's entrance as a group of rowdy adventurers pushes in. "She's got this wall up, especially around anyone who isn't an elf. It's like she's trying to protect something, or prove something to herself. But when it's just us, or with Ellie and Dalan, you see the real Jasira — someone who gives a damn and would probably fight a dragon for the people she cares about." She gives a small shrug. "Just don't ask her about her tribe too often. That's a topic that makes her go colder than a winter in the northern hills."
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie lets out a short, sharp laugh and slaps a hand against the railing, the sound like a crack of thunder. "Trust?" Her one good eye narrows, not with suspicion but with something else — amusement, maybe. "Kid, I don't trust anyone who tells me they're trustworthy. Trust is earned with blood, sweat, and not pissing me off when I'm holding your coin."
*She leans forward, horns catching the lantern light.* "But you've shown more spine than most D-ranks. You took on a job you could've walked away from and didn't run when things got bloody. That counts for something." *A scarred hand comes down on the counter between the exam forms, fingers curled.* "I trust you'll sign those papers if you're got the stones for it. The rest? Well, that's what the exam is for."

Transcript:
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie lets out a short, sharp laugh and slaps a hand against the railing, the sound like a crack of thunder. "Trust?" Her one good eye narrows, not with suspicion but with something else — amusement, maybe. "Kid, I don't trust anyone who tells me they're trustworthy. Trust is earned with blood, sweat, and not pissing me off when I'm holding your coin."
*She leans forward, horns catching the lantern light.* "But you've shown more spine than most D-ranks. You took on a job you could've walked away from and didn't run when things got bloody. That counts for something." *A scarred hand comes down on the counter between the exam forms, fingers curled.* "I trust you'll sign those papers if you're got the stones for it. The rest? Well, that's what the exam is for."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
[8] Domas: Domas looks up from his clipboard, red eyes meeting Max's. He doesn't smile, doesn't offer a patronizing nod. "You owe me nothing." His voice is measured, carrying no weight of expectation. "A life owed is a debt that lingers, and I have no interest in collecting it."
*He straightens the paperwork on the desk, the movement precise and deliberate.* "The road is where debts are forged and settled. What happened there is between you and the world." He pauses, and for a moment the stoic mask wavers just enough to show something underneath—not quite warmth, but an acknowledgement. "I'm simply glad you're here to see what comes next."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
[10] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes mid-step, her serving tray tilting slightly in her grip. The cheerful mask drops, leaving her face open and vulnerable for a heartbeat before she catches herself. She sets the tray down on the nearest table with a softness that belies her surprise, her blue eyes searching Max's face with sudden, sharp intensity.
"Family," Fiana repeats the word quietly, like she's tasting it. A flush creeps up her freckled cheeks, and her expression softens into something that isn't quite a smile — something closer to protective fierce-heartedness. "Well, damn. You don't just say that kind of thing to a barmaid unless you mean it." She steps closer, her voice dropping so it doesn't carry across the hall. "Listen, if that's how it is, then you've got a sister who's going to make sure you don't come back here half-dead or broke. But that means you'd better start taking care of yourself, too, because I won't stand by and watch my family get sloppy."

Transcript:
[11] Max Nightriver (player): Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
[12] Adolion Narrator: Fiana leans against the tavern counter, her blue eyes growing thoughtful. "Honestly?" She lets out a small, rueful laugh. "Jasira doesn't exactly make her feelings easy to read. If you're looking for a straight answer, you might as well be asking a cat to explain its nap schedule."
*She traces a circle in the wood of the bar with one finger, her expression darkening slightly.* "She doesn't hate you, if that's what you're wondering. But she's... prickly. Like a hedgehog that's decided everyone is a threat until proven otherwise." Fiana looks up, her gaze earnest. "To be fair, most of that's not about you. It's about her. She carries herself like she's fighting a war no one else can see, and sometimes that makes her cold to anyone who isn't part of her inner circle."
*A group of rowdy adventurers pushes through the tavern door, their laughter echoing off the timber walls, and Fiana straightens up to resume her barmaid duties.* "The best I can tell you is that she hasn't walked away yet. And with Jasira, that counts for something."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, is Domas your friend, or just someone you work beside?
[14] Vallie: Vallie's one good eye widens for a fraction of a second before she breaks into a roar of laughter that makes the nearby adventurers flinch. "Just work beside? Kid, I've bled with that elf more times than I've had hot meals."
*She reaches back and thumps Domas on the shoulder hard enough to make him stumble forward a step.* "Domas is the only person who's ever kept my head from getting blown off in a dungeon. He's also the only bastard who can tell me I'm being a reckless idiot and not get his teeth knocked in for it." *Her grin is wide and genuine, showing sharp teeth.* "We started in the muck and clawed our way to the top together. That makes us more than friends—that makes us blood. Even if we don't share any."
[15] Domas: Domas catches himself with a subtle shift of weight as Vallie thumps him, the impact barely registered on his stoic expression. "Blood" is a strong word, and one that usually involves a medical professional, but he accepts it with a slight tilt of his head.
*He straightens his vest, the movement almost imperceptible, red eyes glinting with something that might be affection if it weren't so buried under layers of propriety.* "It is a remarkably accurate assessment of our dynamic," he says, his voice dry as aged parchment. "Though I do think the phrase 'reckless idiot' is an understatement when it comes to her approach to diplomacy."

Transcript:
[8] Domas: Domas looks up from his clipboard, red eyes meeting Max's. He doesn't smile, doesn't offer a patronizing nod. "You owe me nothing." His voice is measured, carrying no weight of expectation. "A life owed is a debt that lingers, and I have no interest in collecting it."
*He straightens the paperwork on the desk, the movement precise and deliberate.* "The road is where debts are forged and settled. What happened there is between you and the world." He pauses, and for a moment the stoic mask wavers just enough to show something underneath—not quite warmth, but an acknowledgement. "I'm simply glad you're here to see what comes next."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
[10] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes mid-step, her serving tray tilting slightly in her grip. The cheerful mask drops, leaving her face open and vulnerable for a heartbeat before she catches herself. She sets the tray down on the nearest table with a softness that belies her surprise, her blue eyes searching Max's face with sudden, sharp intensity.
"Family," Fiana repeats the word quietly, like she's tasting it. A flush creeps up her freckled cheeks, and her expression softens into something that isn't quite a smile — something closer to protective fierce-heartedness. "Well, damn. You don't just say that kind of thing to a barmaid unless you mean it." She steps closer, her voice dropping so it doesn't carry across the hall. "Listen, if that's how it is, then you've got a sister who's going to make sure you don't come back here half-dead or broke. But that means you'd better start taking care of yourself, too, because I won't stand by and watch my family get sloppy."
[11] Max Nightriver (player): Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
[12] Adolion Narrator: Fiana leans against the tavern counter, her blue eyes growing thoughtful. "Honestly?" She lets out a small, rueful laugh. "Jasira doesn't exactly make her feelings easy to read. If you're looking for a straight answer, you might as well be asking a cat to explain its nap schedule."
*She traces a circle in the wood of the bar with one finger, her expression darkening slightly.* "She doesn't hate you, if that's what you're wondering. But she's... prickly. Like a hedgehog that's decided everyone is a threat until proven otherwise." Fiana looks up, her gaze earnest. "To be fair, most of that's not about you. It's about her. She carries herself like she's fighting a war no one else can see, and sometimes that makes her cold to anyone who isn't part of her inner circle."
*A group of rowdy adventurers pushes through the tavern door, their laughter echoing off the timber walls, and Fiana straightens up to resume her barmaid duties.* "The best I can tell you is that she hasn't walked away yet. And with Jasira, that counts for something."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, is Domas your friend, or just someone you work beside?
[14] Vallie: Vallie's one good eye widens for a fraction of a second before she breaks into a roar of laughter that makes the nearby adventurers flinch. "Just work beside? Kid, I've bled with that elf more times than I've had hot meals."
*She reaches back and thumps Domas on the shoulder hard enough to make him stumble forward a step.* "Domas is the only person who's ever kept my head from getting blown off in a dungeon. He's also the only bastard who can tell me I'm being a reckless idiot and not get his teeth knocked in for it." *Her grin is wide and genuine, showing sharp teeth.* "We started in the muck and clawed our way to the top together. That makes us more than friends—that makes us blood. Even if we don't share any."
[15] Domas: Domas catches himself with a subtle shift of weight as Vallie thumps him, the impact barely registered on his stoic expression. "Blood" is a strong word, and one that usually involves a medical professional, but he accepts it with a slight tilt of his head.
*He straightens his vest, the movement almost imperceptible, red eyes glinting with something that might be affection if it weren't so buried under layers of propriety.* "It is a remarkably accurate assessment of our dynamic," he says, his voice dry as aged parchment. "Though I do think the phrase 'reckless idiot' is an understatement when it comes to her approach to diplomacy."

She sets the tray down on the nearest table with a softness that belies her surprise, her blue eyes searching Max's face with sudden, sharp intensity.
"Family," Fiana repeats the word quietly, like she's tasting it. A flush creeps up her freckled cheeks, and her expression softens into something that isn't quite a smile — something closer to protective fierce-heartedness. "Well, damn. You don't just say that kind of thing to a barmaid unless you mean it." She steps closer, her voice dropping so it doesn't carry across the hall. "Listen, if that's how it is, then you've got a sister who's going to make sure you don't come back here half-dead or broke. But that means you'd better start taking care of yourself, too, because I won't stand by and watch my family get sloppy."
[11] Max Nightriver (player): Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
[12] Adolion Narrator: Fiana leans against the tavern counter, her blue eyes growing thoughtful. "Honestly?" She lets out a small, rueful laugh. "Jasira doesn't exactly make her feelings easy to read. If you're looking for a straight answer, you might as well be asking a cat to explain its nap schedule."
*She traces a circle in the wood of the bar with one finger, her expression darkening slightly.* "She doesn't hate you, if that's what you're wondering. But she's... prickly. Like a hedgehog that's decided everyone is a threat until proven otherwise." Fiana looks up, her gaze earnest. "To be fair, most of that's not about you. It's about her. She carries herself like she's fighting a war no one else can see, and sometimes that makes her cold to anyone who isn't part of her inner circle."
*A group of rowdy adventurers pushes through the tavern door, their laughter echoing off the timber walls, and Fiana straightens up to resume her barmaid duties.* "The best I can tell you is that she hasn't walked away yet. And with Jasira, that counts for something."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, is Domas your friend, or just someone you work beside?
[14] Vallie: Vallie's one good eye widens for a fraction of a second before she breaks into a roar of laughter that makes the nearby adventurers flinch. "Just work beside? Kid, I've bled with that elf more times than I've had hot meals."
*She reaches back and thumps Domas on the shoulder hard enough to make him stumble forward a step.* "Domas is the only person who's ever kept my head from getting blown off in a dungeon. He's also the only bastard who can tell me I'm being a reckless idiot and not get his teeth knocked in for it." *Her grin is wide and genuine, showing sharp teeth.* "We started in the muck and clawed our way to the top together. That makes us more than friends—that makes us blood. Even if we don't share any."
[15] Domas: Domas catches himself with a subtle shift of weight as Vallie thumps him, the impact barely registered on his stoic expression. "Blood" is a strong word, and one that usually involves a medical professional, but he accepts it with a slight tilt of his head.
*He straightens his vest, the movement almost imperceptible, red eyes glinting with something that might be affection if it weren't so buried under layers of propriety.* "It is a remarkably accurate assessment of our dynamic," he says, his voice dry as aged parchment. "Though I do think the phrase 'reckless idiot' is an understatement when it comes to her approach to diplomacy."
[16] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, I want you at my back on whatever comes next. Partners?
[17] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's hand freezes on the serving tray she's been preparing. She slowly sets it down on the polished wood of the bar, her blue eyes fixing on Max with a depth that wasn't there before. For a moment, the tavern's noise seems to fade into the background—the clatter of mugs, the roar of laughter from the tables, the scrape of boots on floorboards.
"Partners," she repeats softly, and a grin spreads across her face—not the professional smile of a barmaid, but something fiercely personal. "Damn, Max. You don't do things halfway, do you?" She reaches across the counter and grips Max's forearm with surprising strength, her hand warm and steady. "Yeah. Partners. You've got my back, and I've got yours. Always."

Transcript:
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: "Trust is a heavy word, kid." Vallie leans back, crossing her massive arms over her chest. The scars on her forearms shift with the movement, old reminders of old fights. "But yeah. I've watched you work, seen you fight. You've got more steel in you than most folks your age. That's something I can respect."
*She lets out a short, sharp laugh.* "Besides, respect for the Guild is respect for me. You've shown both. Now don't make a liar out of me."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
[8] Domas: "You don't owe me anything," *Domas says, his voice flat and certain, though a faint ghost of a smile touches his lips.* "You survived. That is the only currency the road accepts."
*He adjusts the clipboard in his hand, the movement precise and measured.* "But I appreciate the sentiment. In this building, words like that can be dangerous, so let us keep it between us. The Guild needs results, not debts."
*He looks at the party, red eyes scanning them with clinical detachment.* "Now, we have terms to discuss. Vallie has made her offer. The choice is yours."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
[10] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's hand freezes on the edge of the table she was wiping. Her blue eyes widen, and for a moment she doesn't speak at all, just stares at Max with an expression that shifts from shock to something deeper, softer.
"That's..." She swallows, clearing her throat as if the words are stuck. "That's a hell of a thing to say to a barmaid."
*She lets the rag drop to the table and leans forward, her voice barely above a whisper.* "I... I didn't think anyone in this city would say that to me, not like that."

Transcript:
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: "Trust is a heavy word, kid." Vallie leans back, crossing her massive arms over her chest. The scars on her forearms shift with the movement, old reminders of old fights. "But yeah. I've watched you work, seen you fight. You've got more steel in you than most folks your age. That's something I can respect."
*She lets out a short, sharp laugh.* "Besides, respect for the Guild is respect for me. You've shown both. Now don't make a liar out of me."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
[8] Domas: "You don't owe me anything," *Domas says, his voice flat and certain, though a faint ghost of a smile touches his lips.* "You survived. That is the only currency the road accepts."
*He adjusts the clipboard in his hand, the movement precise and measured.* "But I appreciate the sentiment. In this building, words like that can be dangerous, so let us keep it between us. The Guild needs results, not debts."
*He looks at the party, red eyes scanning them with clinical detachment.* "Now, we have terms to discuss. Vallie has made her offer. The choice is yours."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
[10] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's hand freezes on the edge of the table she was wiping. Her blue eyes widen, and for a moment she doesn't speak at all, just stares at Max with an expression that shifts from shock to something deeper, softer.
"That's..." She swallows, clearing her throat as if the words are stuck. "That's a hell of a thing to say to a barmaid."
*She lets the rag drop to the table and leans forward, her voice barely above a whisper.* "I... I didn't think anyone in this city would say that to me, not like that."
[11] Max Nightriver (player): Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
[12] Adolion Narrator: Fiana lets out a sharp exhale, half-laugh and half-sigh, her curls bouncing as she shakes her head. "Honestly? Most days probably wishes you'd just stop existing so she'd have one less person to avoid."
*She leans her elbows on the table, blue eyes reflecting the tavern's warm amber light.* "Jasira Evergreen doesn't 'get along' with anyone, really. Especially not someone with a Nightriver name and a shadow-magic bent. The Evergreens—her folk—they've got old memories and older grudges."
*Fiana taps a finger against the wooden surface.* "But if you want the truth? She's not just hating on you for sport. She sees something in you that reminds her of people she'd rather not remember. Probably makes her nervous. And when Jasira gets nervous, she gets cold."

*She lets the rag drop to the table and leans forward, her voice barely above a whisper.* "I... I didn't think anyone in this city would say that to me, not like that."

[13] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, is Domas your friend, or just someone you work beside?
[14] Vallie: *Vallie's blue eye widens before a laugh erupts from her chest, sharp and genuine. She slaps a hand against her thigh with enough force to make it sound like a gunshot.* "Work beside? Kid, I'd follow that pointy-eared bastard into the maw of the Lich Queen herself if she tried to claw her way back to life."

[11] Max Nightriver (player): Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
[12] Adolion Narrator: Fiana lets out a sharp exhale, half-laugh and half-sigh, her curls bouncing as she shakes her head. "Honestly? Most days probably wishes you'd just stop existing so she'd have one less person to avoid."
*She leans her elbows on the table, blue eyes reflecting the tavern's warm amber light.* "Jasira Evergreen doesn't 'get along' with anyone, really. Especially not someone with a Nightriver name and a shadow-magic bent. The Evergreens—her folk—they've got old memories and older grudges."
*Fiana taps a finger against the wooden surface.* "But if you want the truth? She's not just hating on you for sport. She sees something in you that reminds her of people she'd rather not remember. Probably makes her nervous. And when Jasira gets nervous, she gets cold."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, is Domas your friend, or just someone you work beside?
[14] Vallie: *Vallie's blue eye widens before a laugh erupts from her chest, sharp and genuine. She slaps a hand against her thigh with enough force to make it sound like a gunshot.* "Work beside? Kid, I'd follow that pointy-eared bastard into the maw of the Lich Queen herself if she tried to claw her way back to life."
*She leans forward, the scars on her arms visible as she gestures broadly toward where Domas stands by the counter.* "We clawed our way from F-rank to A together. Bled in the same gutters, shared the same stale rations. He's the one who kept the paperwork from drowning us while I kept the monsters from eating us."
*Her grin turns a bit more serious, almost fond.* "He's the kind of friend who'll tell you you're an idiot to your face and then throw you his cloak when you're freezing. Best damn partner a woman could ask for."
[15] Domas: *Domas doesn't look up from the clipboard immediately, but there is a subtle softening to his jaw at Vallie's words.* "The Guildmaster is prone to dramatics."
*He finally meets Max's gaze, red eyes calm and measured, though not entirely devoid of warmth.* "We have been through enough together that 'work beside' would be a gross understatement. I have seen her make choices that would make most men sick with fear, and I have trust in those instincts that is absolute."
*He pauses, his expression turning contemplative.* "As for friendship... I find it is a word too easily thrown about in this profession. We are bound by something older and steadier than sentiment. We are comrades. That is more valuable."
[16] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, I want you at my back on whatever comes next. Partners?
[17] Adolion Narrator: *The tavern's warmth seems to pool around Fiana, the amber lantern light catching in her red curls as she processes the offer. Her blue eyes widen, then narrow with a sharp, focused intelligence. The softness of moments ago hardens into something steeled.*
[18] Vallie: *Vallie's blue eye tracks the exchange from the edge of the tavern, one scarred hand resting on her hip. A faint, knowing smirk tugs at the corner of her mouth.* "Well now. That's a bold move for a noble heir."
*She lets out a low whistle, her tone shifting to something more approving.* "Most high-born types in this city wouldn't be caught dead with a barmaid at their back, let alone asking for the partnership. Either you've got a hell of a head on your shoulders, or you're crazier than I thought."
*Her grin widens, showing a glimpse of sharp teeth.* "I like it. Gives this whole rank-up thing some real stakes. A noble and a tavern-worker against the world? That's a story that'll keep the bards in beer for a decade."

[0] Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
[2] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's face lights up, her blue eyes widening as she lets out a delighted laugh. She wipes her hands on her apron and steps forward, closing the distance between them.
"Friend? Oh, I'd call you more than that!" Fiana beams, her freckled cheeks flushing. "You're officially one of my favorite adventurers now. Anyone who can keep their head when things go sideways—and looks half as good doing it—is someone I want in my corner."
She gestures toward the tavern's bar with a grin. "Tavern's on me for the rest of the night. We can celebrate your new rank or your survival, or both—your choice."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
[4] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression softens, a flicker of something complex passing through her eyes before she leans back against the polished wood of the bar. "Jasira?" She swirls the cider in her glass, watching the bubbles rise. "She's... complicated."
"We're friends," Fiana says slowly, "but the kind where you have to walk on eggshells sometimes. She's got a wall around her—high and thick—and most people just give up trying to climb it. Me? I've always liked a challenge." She shrugs, though there's a tension in her shoulders. "She's the best ranger I've ever seen, but there's always this... weight she carries. Like she's waiting for someone to fail her."
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie's blue eye fixes on Max Nightriver, considering, before she lets out a short bark of a laugh. "Kid, you've got the instincts of a predator and the patience of a spider. I've watched you work." She crosses her arms, her black eyepatch shifting as her expression goes serious. "Trust is a heavy word. I don't give it out like beer tokens."
*She leans in closer, her sharp teeth glinting.*
"But I trust you to get the job done. That's what counts in the Guild." A heavy hand lands on Max's shoulder—not too rough, but firm enough to leave a bruise. "Now quit being all sentimental and sign the damned forms before Domas starts chewing my ear about paperwork."

Transcript:
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
[2] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's face lights up, her blue eyes widening as she lets out a delighted laugh. She wipes her hands on her apron and steps forward, closing the distance between them.
"Friend? Oh, I'd call you more than that!" Fiana beams, her freckled cheeks flushing. "You're officially one of my favorite adventurers now. Anyone who can keep their head when things go sideways—and looks half as good doing it—is someone I want in my corner."
She gestures toward the tavern's bar with a grin. "Tavern's on me for the rest of the night. We can celebrate your new rank or your survival, or both—your choice."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
[4] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression softens, a flicker of something complex passing through her eyes before she leans back against the polished wood of the bar. "Jasira?" She swirls the cider in her glass, watching the bubbles rise. "She's... complicated."
"We're friends," Fiana says slowly, "but the kind where you have to walk on eggshells sometimes. She's got a wall around her—high and thick—and most people just give up trying to climb it. Me? I've always liked a challenge." She shrugs, though there's a tension in her shoulders. "She's the best ranger I've ever seen, but there's always this... weight she carries. Like she's waiting for someone to fail her."
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie's blue eye fixes on Max Nightriver, considering, before she lets out a short bark of a laugh. "Kid, you've got the instincts of a predator and the patience of a spider. I've watched you work." She crosses her arms, her black eyepatch shifting as her expression goes serious. "Trust is a heavy word. I don't give it out like beer tokens."
*She leans in closer, her sharp teeth glinting.*
"But I trust you to get the job done. That's what counts in the Guild." A heavy hand lands on Max's shoulder—not too rough, but firm enough to leave a bruise. "Now quit being all sentimental and sign the damned forms before Domas starts chewing my ear about paperwork."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
[8] Domas: Domas pauses mid-turn, his red eyes meeting Max's with an unreadable expression. He slowly lowers the clipboard, setting it on the counter with a soft tap.
"You owe me nothing," he says, his voice measured and quiet enough that only a few nearby can hear. "The road is not a place for debts. If you wish to repay me, then live to see your next rank up." He gives a single, curt nod—a gesture of acknowledgement between equals. "That is all the gratitude I require."
*He retrieves his clipboard and glances at the forms Ellie has laid out, waiting.*

Transcript:
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
[2] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's face lights up, her blue eyes widening as she lets out a delighted laugh. She wipes her hands on her apron and steps forward, closing the distance between them.
"Friend? Oh, I'd call you more than that!" Fiana beams, her freckled cheeks flushing. "You're officially one of my favorite adventurers now. Anyone who can keep their head when things go sideways—and looks half as good doing it—is someone I want in my corner."
She gestures toward the tavern's bar with a grin. "Tavern's on me for the rest of the night. We can celebrate your new rank or your survival, or both—your choice."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
[4] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression softens, a flicker of something complex passing through her eyes before she leans back against the polished wood of the bar. "Jasira?" She swirls the cider in her glass, watching the bubbles rise. "She's... complicated."
"We're friends," Fiana says slowly, "but the kind where you have to walk on eggshells sometimes. She's got a wall around her—high and thick—and most people just give up trying to climb it. Me? I've always liked a challenge." She shrugs, though there's a tension in her shoulders. "She's the best ranger I've ever seen, but there's always this... weight she carries. Like she's waiting for someone to fail her."
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie's blue eye fixes on Max Nightriver, considering, before she lets out a short bark of a laugh. "Kid, you've got the instincts of a predator and the patience of a spider. I've watched you work." She crosses her arms, her black eyepatch shifting as her expression goes serious. "Trust is a heavy word. I don't give it out like beer tokens."
*She leans in closer, her sharp teeth glinting.*
"But I trust you to get the job done. That's what counts in the Guild." A heavy hand lands on Max's shoulder—not too rough, but firm enough to leave a bruise. "Now quit being all sentimental and sign the damned forms before Domas starts chewing my ear about paperwork."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
[8] Domas: Domas pauses mid-turn, his red eyes meeting Max's with an unreadable expression. He slowly lowers the clipboard, setting it on the counter with a soft tap.
"You owe me nothing," he says, his voice measured and quiet enough that only a few nearby can hear. "The road is not a place for debts. If you wish to repay me, then live to see your next rank up." He gives a single, curt nod—a gesture of acknowledgement between equals. "That is all the gratitude I require."
*He retrieves his clipboard and glances at the forms Ellie has laid out, waiting.*

Transcript:
[5] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
[6] Vallie: Vallie's blue eye fixes on Max Nightriver, considering, before she lets out a short bark of a laugh. "Kid, you've got the instincts of a predator and the patience of a spider. I've watched you work." She crosses her arms, her black eyepatch shifting as her expression goes serious. "Trust is a heavy word. I don't give it out like beer tokens."
*She leans in closer, her sharp teeth glinting.*
"But I trust you to get the job done. That's what counts in the Guild." A heavy hand lands on Max's shoulder—not too rough, but firm enough to leave a bruise. "Now quit being all sentimental and sign the damned forms before Domas starts chewing my ear about paperwork."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
[8] Domas: Domas pauses mid-turn, his red eyes meeting Max's with an unreadable expression. He slowly lowers the clipboard, setting it on the counter with a soft tap.
"You owe me nothing," he says, his voice measured and quiet enough that only a few nearby can hear. "The road is not a place for debts. If you wish to repay me, then live to see your next rank up." He gives a single, curt nod—a gesture of acknowledgement between equals. "That is all the gratitude I require."
*He retrieves his clipboard and glances at the forms Ellie has laid out, waiting.*
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
[10] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, soft and heavy. Fiana freezes, her hands still gripped around the rag she'd been using to wipe the bar. Her blue eyes search Max's face, and for a heartbeat, the cheerful mask slips.
"Family..." Fiana breathes the word like it's fragile glass. Her expression softens completely, and she sets the rag down. "You know, most people who come through here just see a barmaid. Someone to pour their drinks and laugh at their jokes." She reaches out, resting her hand briefly over Max's on the cool wood of the bar. "But you actually *see* me."
*She straightens up, a determined look settling on her freckled face.*
"Then you've got a sister in this city now. Someone who'll keep you fed, keep your secrets, and kick your ass if you start acting too much like a brooding hero." Fiana gives his hand a small squeeze before pulling back. "Tavern's still on me tonight. Come on, sit. Tell me what's really going through that head of yours."

[11] Max Nightriver (player): Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
[12] Adolion Narrator: Fiana pauses mid-pour, the cider swirling in her pitcher. She sets it down on the counter with a quiet thud and leans against the bar, her expression growing contemplative.
"Honestly?" Fiana sighs, glancing toward the tavern's entrance as if making sure no one is listening. "She thinks you're a pampered noble who doesn't understand what it means to *earn* something. She sees the Nightriver name and her shoulders tighten up like you've just insulted her ancestors." She drums her fingers on the wood. "But there's more to it. I've seen them in the same room—how she watches you when she thinks you're not looking. It's not just contempt."
*Fiana shakes her head, a wry smile touching her lips.*
"It's like... she recognizes something in you that she doesn't want to admit. Some kind of darkness or weight that matches her own. That's why you clash. She'd rather fight you than face whatever it is that makes her see herself in you." She picks up the pitcher again. "Still, I wouldn't suggest trying to 'get along' with her right now. Just... be patient. Elves like Jasira take a long time to thaw out."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, is Domas your friend, or just someone you work beside?
[14] Vallie: Vallie's blue eye narrows slightly, and she lets out a snort that's half-laugh, half-something else. "Work beside?" She shakes her head, her curved horns catching the light of the Guild's lanterns. "Kid, Domas and I have bled together in more places than I care to count. He's the one who dragged me out of a Zegallan pit when I was too stubborn to die, and I'm the one who punched a mage twice his size in the jaw for thinking he could bully an elf."
*She reaches for a Blackroot cigar from a leather pouch, lighting it with a spark from her thumb.*
"He's the smartest man I know, and the most annoying." A cloud of bitter smoke curls around her face. "But if the world ended tomorrow, Domas is the only person I'd trust to watch my back while I swing my axe. That's more than friendship—that's survival."
[15] Domas: Domas doesn't look up from his clipboard, but the corner of his mouth twitches upward. "I believe the technical term is 'tolerable partnership,' Guildmaster." He finally meets Max's gaze with those piercing red eyes, his expression perfectly composed. "We are bound by history, blood, and an extraordinary amount of paperwork. It would be far too convenient if our relationship were simple."
